title: foreach flattens every item to a string — iterating structured JSON requires re-parsing inside the loop
existing_state: Foreach resolves its collection via `ValueResolver.ResolveCollectionExpression` into a `List<string>` (Services/Scripting/Commands/ForeachCommand.cs:89, 193-196), and the loop variable is set to that string each iteration (ForeachCommand.cs:95). The map form likewise stringifies every value through `JsonUtilities.JsonNodeToStringValue` (ForeachCommand.cs:198-205). So iterating a JSON array of objects — the natural shape of an http/vault/parse result — hands the body a serialized object string, and every field access inside the loop must round-trip through json_get(item, 'field') re-parsing the same string. There is no way to write `{{device.name}}` against the loop variable.
recommendation: Preserve structure through the loop: have ResolveCollection return `List<object?>` keeping JsonNode/dictionary elements intact when the source is a JSON array (strings stay strings, so existing scripts are unaffected), store the element object via context.SetVariable, and make sure the variable-substitution/expression layer supports property access (`item.field` / `{{item.field}}`) on stored object values — json_get can short-circuit on an already-structured value instead of re-parsing. The labelFor truncation (ForeachCommand.cs:96, 48-51) should stringify per-item for iteration-stepper labels as today.
user_benefit: Scripts that iterate API results (interface tables, inventory exports, Vault secret lists) lose a layer of json_get boilerplate per field and a per-access re-parse, making the most common structured-data loop read like every other automation tool (Ansible loop items, PowerShell objects).

evidence.note: items resolved as List<string>; loop var set to items[i] string
ResolveCollection -> ResolveCollectionExpression (strings); map values stringified via JsonNodeToStringValue
